beats.say: A warehouse has 1,000 SQL models. Someone changes one.
What breaks? In which order do you rebuild? And who tests it?
beats.label: The questions
beats.head: What breaks downstream?

beats.say: dbt answers with three things: a graph, incremental models, and tests.
beats.label: Track 9 · dbt

check.prompt: How does dbt know the order to build the models in?
check.why: Each ref is a dependency. dbt builds the graph from them.

beats.say: You write a select statement. dbt wraps it and builds the table for you.
beats.label: A model
beats.head: One select = one model

beats.say: To use another model, you call ref. dbt reads those calls and builds a graph.
beats.label: The graph

beats.say: So dbt knows the order. And it knows what is downstream of a change.
beats.label: Why it matters
beats.head: The graph gives the order

check.prompt: Your incremental model missed rows that arrived late. What do you add?
check.why: Reprocess the last few days on each run, so late rows are picked up.

beats.say: Second: do not rebuild everything each day.
An incremental model processes only the new rows, and merges them in.
beats.label: Incremental
beats.head: Only the new rows

beats.say: The trap is late data. A row arrives two days late, and the filter skips it.
beats.label: The trap
beats.head: Late rows get skipped

beats.say: So look back a few days on each run. And merge on a unique key.
beats.label: The fix
beats.head: A lookback window

beats.say: Third: catch a bad change before it ships.
Data tests check the rows. Unit tests check the logic. A contract fixes the columns.
beats.label: Three layers

beats.say: Start with two tests on every key: unique, and not null.
beats.label: A good start
beats.head: unique + not_null on keys

beats.say: Last: keep a big project fast.
In CI, build only the models that changed, and what depends on them.
beats.label: Slim CI
beats.head: Build only what changed

beats.say: Ref builds the graph. Incremental needs a lookback. And test every key.
beats.label: dbt

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
